data.name: Ohi
data.gender_notes: Ohi is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Ohi is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Ojas', which refers to the vital energy or spirit within an individual. It is believed to represent the divine power residing in all beings. The name Ohi carries the meaning “Divine energy” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Ohi usually hope their child will grow to embody divine energy and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes inner strength, courage, and the divine presence within.
data.etymology: Ohi belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Divine energy.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ohi total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

historical_references.reference: Ohi, a king of the Ikshvaku dynasty, ruled around 15th century BCE in the Kosala kingdom, which is located in the present-day Indian states of Uttar Pradesh and Bihar. He is also known as Vibhishana, and is the younger brother of Ravana. After Ravana's defeat at the hands of Rama, Vibhishana was welcomed into Rama's court, and he became an advisor and aide.

Ohi, a 12th-century CE king of the Chalukya dynasty, ruled in the Karnataka region of present-day India. He is also known as Someshvara I, and is known for his patronage of the Kalyana Chalukyas and the construction of numerous temples, including the famous Kailasa Temple in Ellora.
